title: Latency-Aware Selective Verification in Generate–Validate NetOps Pipelines: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt-5-mini
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (CAND-2026-001) that tests whether inserting a selective, low-latency verification tier (risk scoring + fast validator) into a generate–validate–repair NetOps pipeline reduces unsafe commits from LLM-generated configuration proposals while meeting a latency SLO. Using a deterministic synthetic intent corpus of 400 paired operator intents (10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants), gpt-5-mini as the generator, and a deterministic full-checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) as ground truth, we observed: baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975), guarded (selective verifier) valid = 400/400 (1.000). The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution accounting is artifact-backed: model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial generations + 1 repair) due to the preregistered shared-initial design; all raw outputs, scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes in the execution manifest. The preregistered latency hypothesis (H2, 95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms) could not be evaluated because end-to-end latency telemetry is absent from the archived confirmatory artifacts; this missing telemetry and its provenance are disclosed and artifact-referenced rather than imputed.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation reduces operator effort but raises safety concerns: LLM-generated configuration proposals can be functionally incorrect or introduce regressions. A common mitigation is generate–validate–repair: an LLM proposes a change, a verifier checks functional correctness, and when needed a repair loop is invoked. Full verification can be costly in latency-sensitive settings. We preregistered CAND-2026-001 to evaluate a latency-aware selective-verifier intervention: risk-score shared LLM candidates and send only high-risk proposals to a fast verifier ("guarded" condition), comparing it to an LLM-only baseline in a paired design. The study is fully preregistered; all execution and analysis artifacts are archived and hash-summed (see Disclosure Statement). The core empirical question is whether a selective low-latency verification tier reduces unsafe commits (H1) and whether it meets a latency SLO (H2). The paired design controls for per-intent difficulty and isolates the verifier/repair effect under a shared-initial candidate protocol.
sections.related_work: Recent literature explores LLM-driven configuration generation, verifier-guided repair loops, and agentic NetOps with digital twins and formal checkers (e.g., Cornetto-style configuration-repair benchmarks and agentic verifier-augmented pipelines). These studies show that verifiers reduce regressions but often do not quantify latency-safety trade-offs under operational budgets. Our contribution is a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation that explicitly records execution provenance, reconciles model-call accounting under a shared-initial design, and demonstrates the limits of safety gains when baseline correctness is high.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and experimental design
- Preregistration: study CAND-2026-001 froze research question, confirmatory hypotheses (H1,H2), estimands, sampling plan, retry/missingness rules, and analysis scripts prior to observing outcomes. Preregistration record and SHA-256 are archived (see Disclosure Statement).
- Corpus and tasks: deterministic synthetic intent generator created 400 paired intents covering representative NetOps changes (ACLs, BGP/OSPF route edits, interface edits). Ten percent (40/400) are deterministic adversarial/OOD variants per preregistered perturbation rules. Representative task manifests and reference answers are archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl with SHA-256 entries (see execution manifest).
- Model and calls: declared generator = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json, SHA-256 present). The execution contract set independent_condition_generation=false: the same shared-initial candidate is reused across conditions to isolate verifier/repair effects; this choice was preregistered and deterministically enacted in the run.
- Scoring and validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 acted as full-checker scorer (scoring_rule=full_intent_constraint_validation). Each proposal was scored by the deterministic validator; per-episode scorer JSONs and validator traces are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ with SHA-256 cataloged in the execution manifest.
- Primary estimand and hypothesis tests: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Primary test: exact McNemar two-sided on paired binary outcomes. Confidence intervals: paired bootstrap percentile (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) as preregistered. Secondary estimands (exploratory): verification-budget vs unsafe-commit curve, OOD false-negative rates.
- Execution protocol and reproducibility controls: all model calls, retries, provider traces, and the deterministic reconciliation report are archived with SHA-256 hashes. Missingness/retry policy and infrastructure-failure handling were preregistered and followed; no unrecovered infrastructure failures occurred.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed)
- Completed pairs: 400 (complete_pair_count = 400). See analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA-256: 0d6efc16...)
- Baseline valid proposals: 399/400 (0.9975)
- Guarded valid proposals: 400/400 (1.000)
- Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 399, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. See analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA-256: a6906bb4...)
- Estimand: guarded − baseline = 0.0025. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729).
Execution accounting and reconciliation
- Planned model-call budget in preregistration enumerated 800 calls under an independent-generation accounting convention (400 intents × 2 conditions × 1 generation). The executed run used the preregistered shared-initial design (independent_condition_generation=false): one shared-initial candidate per intent reused across conditions. Observed model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared_initial_generation + 1 repair call). This reconciliation is deterministic and recorded in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json; provider-call audit entries and stage_counts show {"shared_initial_generation":400,"repair":1}; execution_log.jsonl SHA-256: 421f8e68...). The difference (planned 800 vs observed 401) reflects the preregistered choice to share candidates across conditions, not an unlogged rerun.
Representative discordant episode (artifact mapping)
- The single discordant pair (n10 = 1: guarded valid, baseline invalid) is recorded in per-episode scorer JSONs and is available for inspection at execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (artifact paths and hashes listed in the execution manifest). We report only the artifact locations here; the archived validator traces show the baseline proposal failed a required dependency check while the guarded pipeline either repaired or selected a corrected candidate prior to final scoring (see execution/scoring/task-000149-*.json in archive).
Missing preregistered telemetry (H2)
- Preregistered H2 required end-to-end pipeline latency telemetry (95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms). The confirmatory artifact bundle does not include end-to-end latency traces or telemetry files, preventing artifact-backed evaluation of H2. The absence is recorded in execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA-256s in the execution manifest). We therefore report H2 as unresolved in this run rather than imputing timing.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and operational implications
- Safety effect size and ceiling effect: baseline correctness against the deterministic validator was near ceiling (399/400). Under such conditions the marginal safety gain achievable by adding a selective fast verifier is necessarily small; the observed absolute gain (0.25 percentage points) is artifact-backed but not statistically distinguishable from zero given the discordance pattern (n10=1, n01=0) and the exact McNemar test result. This ceiling effect is an expected threat to internal power and is discussed as a limitation below.
- Shared-initial design trade-off: the preregistered shared-initial protocol reduces variance due to stochastic generation and isolates verifier/repair impact, but it conditions the estimand on a single generated candidate per intent; therefore the reported paired difference quantifies verifier/repair efficacy conditional on that shared candidate rather than the joint effect of independently generated alternative candidates plus verification. The design choice materially reduced model call counts (401 observed calls) and should be considered when interpreting generalization to workflows where independent generation per approval path is required.
- When guarded verification helps: in environments where baseline LLM generation performance is lower, validators disagree more often, or adversarial/OOD inputs are frequent, selective verification with calibrated risk thresholds is likely to yield larger safety gains. The preregistered set of exploratory analyses (threshold sweeps, OOD subgroup analysis) are recommended next steps using the same artifact pipelines and are fully supported by the stored scoring and provider-call traces.
- Reproducibility: all numbers and reconciliations above are traceable to archived artifacts (per-episode scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider-call logs, execution manifest). Key artifact hashes and paths are recorded in the Disclosure Statement for independent verification.
- Latency unresolved: because the run did not include end-to-end latency telemetry, operational feasibility (H2) remains an open question for this run. Future runs must record detailed pipeline timing (timestamps for shared-initial generation, risk-scoring, fast verifier, full-checker) to test latency targets and report verified SLO compliance.
Threats to validity (summary)
- Internal validity: preregistered shared-initial design conditions estimand; generator nondeterminism avoided by design; no unrecovered infrastructure failures occurred; provider nondeterminism could still influence token-level outputs but the shared-initial reuse minimizes its effect.
- Construct validity: the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 models intended operational correctness but is an abstraction (digital-twin semantics); real-device behavior may differ.
- External validity: single model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic intent corpus limit generalization to other LLMs, real operator language, and production diversity.
- Conclusion validity: near-ceiling baseline rate reduces power to detect small safety gains; paired bootstrap CI and exact McNemar p-value quantify this uncertainty artifact-backed.
Recommendations for follow-up studies (artifact-grounded)
1) Include end-to-end latency telemetry in the artifact bundle and preregister latency analysis scripts to evaluate H2. 2) Repeat with independent_condition_generation=true (independent generations per condition) to measure joint generation+verifier effects; record both model-call budgets and observed provider-call logs. 3) Sweep selective-verifier risk-thresholds on larger adversarial/OOD subsets to map verification-budget vs unsafe-commit Pareto frontiers. 4) Test multiple LLMs and validators to assess external generality; all artifacts and scorer JSONs should be archived as done here.
sections.conclusion: This preregistered, artifact-backed paired study found a small absolute safety gain (0.25 percentage points) for a selective low-latency verification intervention over an LLM-only baseline on a deterministic synthetic NetOps corpus; the difference is numerically small, and inference is constrained by a near-ceiling baseline and the shared-initial design. Crucially, the preregistered latency SLO (H2) could not be evaluated from the archived artifacts because end-to-end latency telemetry was not recorded; we disclose this absence and provide full execution provenance for independent inspection. All raw outputs, validator traces, per-episode scorer JSONs, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes in the execution manifest to enable reproducibility and follow-up experiments that address the outlined limitations and open questions.

The provider-call audit in execution/execution_manifest.json documents stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 400, "repair": 1}, condition_counts = {"shared": 400, "guarded": 1}, and provider call logs are archived under execution/provider_calls/ (many per-episode JSONs with SHA-256 values recorded). Key execution artifacts: execution/execution_log.jsonl (SHA-256: 421f8e6830833211c929e586804e79cb1a001eb8d6a550d0ac19efbc8a979753) and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA-256: 9ea0d56d48a5cc7ff198d85d0a12c21536fab716c042bd5eb2033492eda5b18e).
- Planned vs observed model calls: the preregistration budget listed planned_model_calls = 800 under independent-generation accounting. The executed shared-initial design (independent_condition_generation=false) was preregistered and produced 400 shared-initial generations plus one repair call, giving model_calls_used = 401; this deterministic reconciliation is recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (artifact archived).

The confirmatory artifact bundle does not contain the required latency telemetry files; this absence is recorded in the execution logs. - Human involvement: no manual editing of the technical manuscript text or analysis occurred after the autonomy lock. Pre-lock human activity was limited to selecting the topic family and initial prompt constraints; pre-lock infrastructure development is explicitly excluded from the confirmatory evidence unless recreated post-lock (it was not).
- Reproducibility: all raw outputs, per-episode scorer JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), response texts (execution/responses/*.txt), provider-call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), task and transformation manifests, model configuration, result schema, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA-256 hashes and paths in the execution manifest; these enable deterministic verification of the reported numbers. - Limitations and provenance: (i) single model (gpt-5-mini) and single deterministic validator; (ii) synthetic corpus; (iii) shared-initial design conditions estimand; (iv) absent end-to-end latency telemetry for H2. All are disclosed above and discussed in the manuscript Limitations section.
limitations: Synthetic confirmatory corpus: tasks were generated deterministically and may not reflect production linguistic diversity or operator phrasing.
Single LLM: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize to other foundation models without further testing.
Single deterministic validator: safety labels derive from deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (digital-twin semantics); real-device divergences are possible.

Shared-initial design: independent_condition_generation=false was preregistered and isolates verifier effects conditional on a single generated candidate; it narrows the estimand relative to independent-generation workflows.
Latency SLO unresolved: required end-to-end latency telemetry for H2 was not present in archived confirmatory artifacts; H2 could not be evaluated from this run.
